title: A pseudovirus-based neutralizing antibody assay for measuring neutralizing antibody against rabies virus
abstract: ABSTRACT To establish a laboratory detection assay for a human neutralizing antibody (NAb) against rabies virus and to evaluate its efficiency in human serum samples. A pseudovirus pXN2‐RABV‐G harboring the RABV G gene was applied. The precision, robustness, linearity, stability, inclusivity, and limit of detection of the assay were evaluated. The consistency and correlation of the assay with ELISA and rapid fluorescent focus inhibition test (RFFIT) were analyzed. A pseudovirus-based neutralizing antibody (pVNA) detection system based on the pXN2‐RABV‐G was successfully developed and showed broad robustness (culture media: χ 2 = 4.00, P > 0.05, cell passages: χ 2 = 0.25, P > 0.05), precision (independent detection: P > 0.05), lower/upper limit of linearity (0.09 to 93.73 IU/mL, R 2 > 0.95), and stability ( P > 0.05). The limit of detection (LOD) was 2.63 IU/mL (95% CI: 1.81–3.84), expressed as the lowest human sera antibody level reliably distinguishable from background signals, and the coefficient of variation was less than 20%. Compared with the commercial ELISA and the gold standard RFFIT assay, the kappa values were 0.74 and 0.82, respectively, and the results were highly consistent. Linear correlation analysis revealed a strong correlation between these variables ( R 2 > 0.90). A total of 103 recipients from 2019 to 2023 were included in the serological testing and the following analysis. NAb titers were significantly correlated with vaccine dose ( P < 0.001) and the most recent vaccination time ( P < 0.001). The geometric mean titer (GMT) of the 5-dose vaccination group was greater than that of the 1-dose, 2-dose, 3-dose, and 4-dose groups (3.15 vs 3.19 vs 6.18 vs 12.21 vs 13.40 IU/mL). The established pVNA assay for human rabies NAb detection has a detection capability similar to that of the gold standard RFFIT, but it has the advantages of reduced biosafety requirements, laboratory activity, and time, which highlight its safety, high efficiency, and feasibility for screening and monitoring rabies virus antibodies after vaccination. IMPORTANCE Rabies is a lethal disease with no effective clinical treatment. Vaccination is the only way to prevent it routinely, which makes post-vaccination antibody testing essential. The current standard test requires a highly equipped laboratory, biosafety measures, and is time-consuming. This study develops a safe, efficient test for detecting rabies neutralizing antibodies using pseudovirus technology. It is comparable to the gold standard test in accuracy but easier to implement in routine labs, which enables broader use in screening and monitoring antibodies post-vaccination. This advantage addresses a key gap in rabies prevention, reducing the uncertainty for individuals with immunodeficiency who are nonresponsive to vaccination and at risk of rabies exposure.

The limit of detection (LOD) was 2.63 IU/mL (95% CI: 1.81–3.84), expressed as the lowest human sera antibody level reliably distinguishable from background signals, and the coefficient of variation was less than 20%. Compared with the commercial ELISA and the gold standard RFFIT assay, the kappa values were 0.74 and 0.82, respectively, and the results were highly consistent. Linear correlation analysis revealed a strong correlation between these variables ( R 2 > 0.90). A total of 103 recipients from 2019 to 2023 were included in the serological testing and the following analysis. NAb titers were significantly correlated with vaccine dose ( P < 0.001) and the most recent vaccination time ( P < 0.001). The geometric mean titer (GMT) of the 5-dose vaccination group was greater than that of the 1-dose, 2-dose, 3-dose, and 4-dose groups (3.15 vs 3.19 vs 6.18 vs 12.21 vs 13.40 IU/mL). IMPORTANCE Rabies is a lethal disease with no effective clinical treatment. Vaccination is the only way to prevent it routinely, which makes post-vaccination antibody testing essential. The current standard test requires a highly equipped laboratory, biosafety measures, and is time-consuming. This study develops a safe, efficient test for detecting rabies neutralizing antibodies using pseudovirus technology. It is comparable to the gold standard test in accuracy but easier to implement in routine labs, which enables broader use in screening and monitoring antibodies post-vaccination. title: Analysis of the current status of animal-related injuries in the Taihu Lake region: a quality assessment of post-exposure prophylaxis in 40,222 Cases (2023–2025) and implications for areas with no reported indigenous human rabies cases
abstract: Abstract Background The Taihu Lake region, a highly urbanized area in the Yangtze River Delta, experiences a high prevalence of animal‐related injuries. Within this region, Wuxi has reported no indigenous human rabies cases for over a decade. Against China’s 2024–2025 rabies resurgence, any decline in post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) quality in zero-case areas could become a weak link that ignites epidemic resurgence. This study evaluated first-visit PEP quality in the region, explored the possible risk of what we term “prevention fatigue”—a silent decline in PEP quality in areas with no reported indigenous human rabies cases—and proposed targeted intervention strategies. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, we included 40,222 first‐visit cases of animal‐related injuries at our hospital from January 2023 to December 2025. Outcomes included non-use of passive immunization in Grade III exposures, failure of standard first-visit care, and delayed presentation. Multivariable logistic regression examined associations and interaction effects. Results Grade III exposures accounted for 60.5% (24,322/40,222) of all cases. Among these, the passive immunization rate was 55.5%, and the standard first‐visit care rate was 45.3% (11,019/24,322). Young adults (15–44 years, aOR = 2.17), scratches (vs. bites, aOR = 1.20), and delayed presentation (aOR = 1.49) were independently associated with incomplete PEP delivery. Significant interactions were found for age group × injury type ( P < 0.001), animal × delayed presentation ( P < 0.001), and exposure site × delayed presentation ( P = 0.019). From 2023 to 2025, passive immunization rates among Grade III exposures increased from 52.8% to 60.1% (P for trend < 0.001), whereas standard first-visit care rates were 44.5%, 42.8%, and 48.4% across the three years (P for trend < 0.001); delayed presentation decreased from 37.9% to 31.9% (P for trend < 0.001). Conclusions Persistent gaps in PEP compliance were observed in this region with over a decade of no indigenous human rabies cases. Young adults, patients with scratch injuries and delayed consultation constituted overlapping high-risk groups. We put forward two sentinel surveillance indicators and stratified intervention strategies, stressing that Grade III scratches require the same protective management as bite wounds.

Against China’s 2024–2025 rabies resurgence, any decline in post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) quality in zero-case areas could become a weak link that ignites epidemic resurgence. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, we included 40,222 first‐visit cases of animal‐related injuries at our hospital from January 2023 to December 2025. Outcomes included non-use of passive immunization in Grade III exposures, failure of standard first-visit care, and delayed presentation. Multivariable logistic regression examined associations and interaction effects. Results Grade III exposures accounted for 60.5% (24,322/40,222) of all cases. Among these, the passive immunization rate was 55.5%, and the standard first‐visit care rate was 45.3% (11,019/24,322). Young adults (15–44 years, aOR = 2.17), scratches (vs. bites, aOR = 1.20), and delayed presentation (aOR = 1.49) were independently associated with incomplete PEP delivery. Significant interactions were found for age group × injury type ( P P P = 0.019). analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the quality of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in the Taihu Lake region, where animal-related injuries are prevalent and there has been no indigenous human rabies cases for over a decade.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 40,222 first-visit cases of animal-related injuries at a hospital in the Taihu Lake region from January 2023 to December 2025.
analysis.methods: Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine associations and interaction effects between risk factors and incomplete PEP delivery, while outcomes included non-use of passive immunization in Grade III exposures, failure of standard first-visit care, and delayed presentation.
analysis.main_results: Grade III exposures accounted for 60.5% (24,322/40,222) of all cases, with a passive immunization rate of 55.5% and a standard first-visit care rate of 45.3% (11,019/24,322). Young adults (15–44 years), patients with scratch injuries, and those with delayed presentation were independently associated with incomplete PEP delivery.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that persistent gaps in PEP compliance in areas with no reported indigenous human rabies cases could pose a risk for future outbreaks, highlighting the concept of prevention fatigue.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the need for targeted surveillance and intervention strategies to address PEP compliance in high-risk groups, particularly in regions with no indigenous human rabies cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential biases in self-reported data, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the quality of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in the Taihu Lake region, where animal-related injuries are common and there have been no indigenous human rabies cases for over a decade. The research highlights the risk of prevention fatigue in zero-case areas and identifies young adults, scratch injuries, and delayed presentation as independent risk factors for incomplete PEP delivery. The authors propose targeted surveillance and intervention strategies, emphasizing that Grade III scratches require the same protective management as bite wounds. The study's large sample size and statistical methods provide strong evidence, though its retrospective design may introduce biases. These findings have important implications for maintaining PEP compliance in regions with no reported rabies cases, potentially preventing future outbreaks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估太湖地区 暴露后预防 (PEP) 的质量,该地区动物相关伤害盛行,并且十多年来没有本土人类 暴露后预防 病例。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性横断面研究纳入了 2023 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月太湖地区一家医院的 40,222 例初诊动物相关伤害病例。
elements_zh.methods: 使用多变量逻辑回归来检查危险因素与不完整 PEP 实施之间的关联和交互作用,而结果包括在 III 级暴露中不使用被动免疫、标准首次就诊护理失败以及延迟就诊。
elements_zh.main_results: III级暴露占所有病例的60.5%(24,322/40,222),被动免疫率为55.5%,标准初诊护理率为45.3%(11,019/24,322)。年轻人(15-44 岁)、有抓伤的患者以及就诊延迟的患者与不完整的 PEP 给药独立相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,在没有报告土著人类 狂犬病 病例的地区,PEP 合规性方面持续存在的差距可能会对未来的 狂犬病 构成风险,这凸显了预防疲劳的概念。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要有针对性的 狂犬病 和干预策略来解决高危人群的 PEP 合规问题,特别是在没有本土人类 狂犬病 病例的地区。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和自我报告数据的潜在偏差而受到限制,但由于样本量大和统计分析,证据是强有力的。

title: Atypical neuroimaging in rabies encephalitis: A case report of concurrent cerebral venous sinus thrombosis in a nine-year-old patient
abstract: Human rabies is a fatal viral encephalitis that presents a profound diagnostic challenge in the absence of a known history of animal exposure. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation and hydrophobia, despite no reported history of an animal bite or scratch. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) served as a critical diagnostic tool, strongly suggesting rabies encephalitis by revealing classic bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes. Concurrently, MRI revealed an atypical and rare macrovascular finding: extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis of the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses, which likely accounted for additional asymmetric white matter changes. A nuchal skin biopsy analyzed via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction confirmed the presence of rabies virus RNA. Despite aggressive neurocritical care and therapeutic anticoagulation, the patient’s condition deteriorated, and he passed away on day 9 of admission. This case underscores the dual role of MRI in acute encephalitis: guiding early etiological diagnosis of rabies and identifying concurrent, clinically significant macrovascular complications like cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.

title: Factors associated with rabies vaccination uptake among dog owners in Butaleja Town Council, Eastern Uganda: A cross-sectional study
abstract: ABSTRACT Rabies remains a major zoonotic public health threat, associated with approximately 59,000 annual deaths globally, with Africa bearing 36% of this burden. In Uganda, an estimated 36 human deaths and 1.8 million dog bite exposures occur annually, yet national dog vaccination coverage remains critically low at approximately 10%. This study investigated factors associated with rabies vaccination uptake among dog owners in Butaleja Town Council, Eastern Uganda, a high-risk setting. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 173 dog owners between May 18 and June 28, 2024, using semi-structured questionnaires. The primary outcome was vaccination uptake (≥1 dose in the past year). Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimated adjusted prevalence ratios for all socio-demographic, veterinary system, health system, dog-related, and knowledge factors. Among 173 dog owners, 57.2% vaccinated at least one dog, corresponding to 54.6% (166/304) of all dogs vaccinated. Factors associated with vaccination uptake included older age (21–40 years: aPR 1.43, 95% CI: 1.15–1.71; 41–60 years: aPR 1.53, 95% CI: 1.22–1.82; ≥61 years: aPR 1.56, 95% CI: 1.33–2.23), higher education (primary: aPR 1.20, 95% CI: 1.00–1.45; secondary: aPR 1.55, 95% CI: 1.20–2.00), higher income, access to veterinary clinics (aPR 2.50, 95% CI: 1.52–3.75), and participation in community education sessions (aPR 1.71, 95% CI: 1.34–2.15). While household-level uptake showed moderate engagement, the resulting dog population vaccination coverage of 48.4% remained substantially below the 70% World Health Organization threshold required for herd immunity. Achieving the “Zero by 30” elimination dog-bite mediated Rabies target in this setting requires targeted interventions addressing the identified associated factors including; enhanced community education, improved veterinary service accessibility, reminder systems, and strategies to convert partial household vaccination into complete coverage particularly among younger, less educated, and lower-income dog owners. Author Summary Rabies remains a neglected tropical disease that claims approximately 59,000 lives annually, predominantly in Africa and Asia. While mass dog vaccination is the most effective control strategy, many communities struggle to reach the 70% coverage needed to mitigate rabies transmission. This study investigated why dog owners in a high-risk Ugandan community do or do not vaccinate their animals. We surveyed 173 dog owners and found an important gap; while 57% of owners had vaccinated at least one dog, only 48% of all dogs were actually vaccinated far below the global target. This distinction matters because it shows that even owners who participate in vaccination programs often leave some dogs unprotected, undermining efforts to achieve herd immunity. Several factors were associated with vaccination. Owners with better access to veterinary clinics, knowledge of where to get vaccines, and participation in community education were more likely to vaccinate. Receiving vaccination reminders also made a significant difference. Conversely, limited awareness, poor service accessibility, and socioeconomic challenges prevented many from vaccinating their dogs. These findings point to practical solutions: improving communication about vaccination locations, sending reminders, and strengthening community education could help more families fully vaccinate all their dogs. For Uganda and similar settings, addressing these barriers is essential to reach the global goal of eliminating rabies deaths by 2030.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究旨在调查乌干达东部布塔莱贾镇议会(高风险地区)的狗主人对 狂犬病 疫苗接种 吸收的相关因素。重点是了解该社区中 疫苗接种 行为的决定因素,以改进 狂犬病 控制工作。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 2024年5月18日至6月28日期间,使用半结构化问卷对173名狗主人进行了横断面调查。使用具有稳健方差的修正泊松回归来估计影响 疫苗接种 吸收的因素的调整后的 患病率 比率。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,狗主人对 疫苗接种 的吸收率为 57.2%,相当于所有接种疫苗的狗的 48.4%。与 疫苗接种 率较高相关的因素包括年龄较大、受教育程度较高、收入较高、前往兽医诊所的机会以及参与社区教育课程。这些发现强调了解决社会经济和无障碍障碍以提高 疫苗接种 覆盖率的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究指出,家庭层面的 疫苗接种 吸收率与实际狗种群覆盖率之间存在差距,该覆盖率仍远低于 WHO 70% 的群体免疫阈值。主人参与率和狗 疫苗接种 率之间的区别强调了采取有针对性的干预措施以确保完全覆盖的必要性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 为了实现“30 年前零”消灭由狗咬伤引起的 狂犬病 的目标,该研究建议加强社区教育,改善兽医服务的可及性,实施提醒系统,并解决年轻、受教育程度较低和收入较低的狗主人的障碍。这些策略可以帮助提高 疫苗接种 对社区中所有狗的全面覆盖。

title: Community engagement strategies for preventing recurrent Nipah virus outbreaks in Bangladesh and India: adapting a framework for outbreak preparedness and response.
abstract: The Nipah virus (NiV) infection is a highly fatal zoonotic disease with pandemic potential which has led to recurrent outbreaks in Bangladesh and India. While transmission pathways, including contaminated date palm sap and human-to-human spread, are increasingly identified, significant uncertainties remain. With no approved therapeutics or vaccines, prevention depends on addressing ecological and behavioural drivers of transmission. This viewpoint draws on selected evidence from NiV outbreaks and response to other zoonotic disease epidemics, such as Ebola, rabies, and the Marburg virus disease, we seek to foster discussion on why community engagement could be central to NiV prevention and preparedness. We highlight the relevance of community engagement through a spectrum of its intensity, which distinguishes between community-oriented, community-based, community-managed, and community-owned approaches. Adapting an existing model, we discuss how community engagement principles can be applied to tackle recurring NiV outbreaks in Bangladesh and India. By aligning interventions with sociocultural realities, community engagement can improve acceptability, enhance early detection, strengthen outbreak response, and support preparedness for future vaccine and therapeutic research. However, evidence specific to NiV remains limited and lessons from other diseases should be applied judiciously. In the absence of medical countermeasures, participatory, locally grounded approaches offer a sustainable pathway to reduce recurrent outbreaks and prevent future spillover events.

abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 感染是一种高度致命的人畜共患疾病,具有大流行潜力,已导致孟加拉国和印度反复出现 暴发。虽然 传播 途径(包括受污染的枣椰树液和人际传播)越来越多地被确定,但仍然存在重大不确定性。由于没有批准的治疗方法或 疫苗,预防取决于解决 疫苗 的生态和行为驱动因素。这一观点借鉴了 NiV 暴发 的精选证据以及对其他人畜共患疾病流行病(例如埃博拉、狂犬病 和马尔堡病毒病)的反应,我们寻求促进关于为什么社区参与可能成为 NiV 预防和准备的核心的讨论。我们通过一系列强度来强调社区参与的相关性,这区分了面向社区、基于社区、社区管理和社区所有的方法。我们采用现有模型,讨论如何应用社区参与原则来解决孟加拉国和印度反复出现的 NiV 暴发 问题。通过使干预措施与社会文化现实相结合,社区参与可以提高可接受性,增强早期发现,加强 疫苗 反应,并支持为未来的 疫苗 和治疗研究做好准备。然而,针对 NiV 的证据仍然有限,应谨慎应用其他疾病的经验教训。在缺乏医疗对策的情况下,参与性、立足当地的方法提供了一条可持续的途径,以减少 暴发 的复发并预防未来的 跨物种溢出 事件。

title: Immunogenicity in dogs vaccinated against rabies with a highly safe and efficacious 3rd generation oral rabies vaccine in longitudinal and cross-sectional studies
abstract: Although oral vaccination of dogs against rabies is considered a promising and beneficial approach, the effectiveness of oral rabies vaccines inducing a protective (humoral) immune response in local free-roaming dogs is often questioned. To address concerns regarding this issue, an analysis was conducted to evaluate the immunogenicity and serological response to the oral rabies vaccine strain SPBN GASGAS in dogs. Serological data from longitudinal and cross-sectional studies conducted under both experimental and field conditions were analysed. Factors influencing the post-vaccination serological response, including bait matrix, sachet type, vaccine titre, and dog origin, were compared, and challenges and limitations in the serological assessment of oral vaccination in dog populations were examined. In addition, the kinetics of rabies virus-binding antibodies following vaccination were analysed and interpreted in the context of SPBN GASGAS-induced rabies-specific immunoglobulin classes. The analyses demonstrate that free-roaming dogs, irrespective of origin, develop a measurable, consistent, and long-lasting humoral immune response following vaccination with SPBN GASGAS. This response is comparable to that observed in dogs under experimental conditions and non-inferior to that induced by parenteral administration of inactivated rabies vaccines. These findings highlight the substantial potential of oral vaccination of free-roaming dogs as a complementary tool within integrated rabies elimination programmes.

abstract_zh: 尽管口服 狂犬病 狗对抗 狂犬病 被认为是一种有前途且有益的方法,但口服 狂犬病 疫苗 在当地自由漫游的狗中诱导保护性(体液)免疫应答 的有效性经常受到质疑。为了解决有关此问题的担忧,进行了一项分析,以评估口服 狂犬病 疫苗 菌株 SPBN GASGAS 在狗中的免疫原性和血清学反应。分析了在实验和现场条件下进行的纵向和横断面研究的血清学数据。比较了影响 疫苗 后血清学反应的因素,包括诱饵基质、小袋类型、疫苗 滴度和狗的来源,并检查了狗群中口服 疫苗 血清学评估的挑战和局限性。此外,在 SPBN GASGAS 诱导的 狂犬病 特异性免疫球蛋白类别的背景下,对 疫苗接种 后的 狂犬病病毒 结合抗体的动力学进行了分析和解释。分析表明,自由漫游的狗,无论其来源如何,在使用 SPBN GASGAS 进行 疫苗接种 后,都会产生可测量的、一致的且持久的体液 免疫应答。该反应与在实验条件下在狗中观察到的反应相当,并且不劣于通过肠胃外施用灭活的狂犬病 疫苗诱导的反应。这些发现凸显了自由漫游狗口服 疫苗接种 作为综合 狂犬病 消除计划中的补充工具的巨大潜力。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述分析了在实验和现场条件下进行的纵向和横断面研究的血清学数据。这些研究评估了狗对 SPBN GASGAS 疫苗 菌株的免疫原性和血清学反应。该审查没有明确报告所使用的数据库、检索日期或资格标准,但包含了来自多个研究设计的数据。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 分析表明,自由漫游的狗,无论其来源如何,在使用 SPBN GASGAS 进行 疫苗接种 后,都会产生可测量的、一致的且持久的体液 免疫应答。该反应与在实验条件下在狗中观察到的反应相当,并且不劣于通过肠胃外施用灭活的狂犬病 疫苗诱导的反应。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 比较了影响 疫苗 后血清学反应的因素,如诱饵基质、小袋类型、疫苗 滴度和狗来源。然而,该综述没有提供有关反应异质性的详细信息,也没有提供与口服 狂犬病 疫苗 在当地自由漫游狗群中的有效性相关的具体证据差距的详细信息。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调了自由漫游狗口服 疫苗接种 作为综合 狂犬病 消除计划中的补充工具的巨大潜力。该综述还强调需要检查犬群中口服 疫苗接种 血清学评估的挑战和局限性。

title: An experimental multiplex PCR/RT-PCR for detection of the main viruses associated with equine neurological disease.
abstract: Viral neurological infections are important causes of morbidity and mortality in horses worldwide. Herein, we describe an end-point multiplex PCR/RT-PCR for simultaneous and differential detection of major equine encephalitis-related agents: rabies virus (RABV), equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), alphaviruses [Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), Eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV), Western equine encephalitis virus (WEEV) and Madariaga virus (MADV)] and flaviviruses [West Nile virus (WNV), Saint Louis encephalitis virus (SLEV), Rocio virus (ROCV) and Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV)]. The multiplex assay successfully amplified all targets either individually or simultaneously: alphavirus (381 bp-experimentally evaluated for MADV and potentially applicable to EEEV and WEEV based on primer design and sequence conservation), EHV-1 (255 bp), RABV (173 bp), VEEV (119 bp), and flavivirus (97-101 bp-experimentally evaluated using ROCV, with the potential to also detect WNV, SLEV and JEV, based on primer design and sequence conservation). Furthermore, the assay demonstrated analytical sensitivity and specificity that support its use for the comprehensive etiological diagnosis of equine neurological diseases. Overall, the multiplex PCR/RT-PCR described here may contribute to the diagnosis of viral neurological infections in horses, reducing costs and turnaround time, while contributing to prevention and control measures.

The assay successfully amplified all targets, demonstrating analytical sensitivity and specificity that support its use in comprehensive etiological diagnosis. The study contributes to the development of diagnostic tools for equine neurological diseases, which has implications for surveillance and prevention. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在此,我们描述了用于同时和差异检测主要马脑炎相关病原体的终点多重 PCR/RT-PCR:狂犬病病毒 (RABV)、马疱疹病毒 1 型 (EHV-1)、甲病毒 [委内瑞拉马脑炎病毒 (VEEV)、东部马脑炎病毒 (EEEV)、西部马脑炎病毒 (WEEV) 和马达里亚加病毒(MADV)]和黄病毒[西尼罗河病毒(WNV)、圣路易斯脑炎病毒(SLEV)、罗西奥病毒(ROCV)和日本脑炎病毒(JEV)]。
elements_zh.methods: 多重检测成功地单独或同时扩增了所有靶标:甲病毒(381 bp,针对 MADV 进行了实验评估,根据引物设计和序列保守性,可能适用于 EEEV 和 WEEV)、EHV-1 (255 bp)、RABV (173 bp)、VEEV (119 bp) 和黄病毒(97-101 bp,使用 ROCV 进行了实验评估,也有可能检测到WNV、SLEV 和 JEV,基于引物设计和序列保存)。
elements_zh.main_results: 此外,该测定法表现出分析灵敏度和特异性,支持其用于马神经系统疾病的综合病因学 诊断。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总体而言,本文描述的多重 PCR/RT-PCR 可能有助于马匹病毒神经感染的 诊断,降低成本和周转时间,同时有助于预防和控制措施。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为开发针对 狂犬病病毒 和其他马神经病原体的更有效的诊断工具提供信息,支持改进的 监测 和马健康管理策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告 狂犬病病毒 检测方法的局限性或证据强度。

The multiplex assay successfully amplified all targets either individually or simultaneously: alphavirus (381 bp-experimentally evaluated for MADV and potentially applicable to EEEV and WEEV based on primer design and sequence conservation), EHV-1 (255 bp), RABV (173 bp), VEEV (119 bp), and flavivirus (97-101 bp-experimentally evaluated using ROCV, with the potential to also detect WNV, SLEV and JEV, based on primer design and sequence conservation). Furthermore, the assay demonstrated analytical sensitivity and specificity that support its use for the comprehensive etiological diagnosis of equine neurological diseases. Overall, the multiplex PCR/RT-PCR described here may contribute to the diagnosis of viral neurological infections in horses, reducing costs and turnaround time, while contributing to prevention and control measures.

title: One Health Prioritization of Rabies Risk in the Republic of Guinea: Integration of Human Knowledge, Canine Immunity, and Spatial Analysis
abstract: Background: Dog-mediated rabies remains a fatal but preventable zoonosis. Its elimination requires sufficient canine vaccination coverage, informed communities, and spatially targeted surveillance. In Guinea, human knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) data and canine serological data had previously been analyzed separately, limiting their translation into operational priorities. Objective: To build an integrated One Health assessment of rabies risk by combining KAP indicators, canine immunity, and spatial analysis. Methods: A secondary integrated analysis was conducted using a KAP survey of 2733 respondents and canine rabies serology from 419 vaccinated dogs tested with the PlateliaTM Rabies II ELISA, with a protection threshold set at 0.5 IU/mL. Indicators were regionalized, compared, and incorporated into a vulnerability index. Associations were estimated by logistic regression with 95% confidence intervals, and spatial findings were displayed on a real map of Guinea. Results: Knowledge was insufficient or intermediate among most respondents, unfavorable attitudes reached 88.84%, and poor practices reached 73.80%. Declared canine vaccination coverage remained below the 70% programmatic threshold in all regions. Overall canine seroprotection was high (88.78%), but 11.22% of dogs remained insufficiently protected. Among dog owners, knowledge of rabies was associated with dog vaccination (OR = 2.77; 95% CI: 1.49–6.29). The integrated One Health assessment ranked Kindia as priority 1, Siguiri as priority 2, Boké and Labé as priority 3, and N’Zérékoré as priority 4. Conclusions: The integrated analysis shows that a strong immune response among vaccinated dogs is not sufficient when coverage, human practices, and the spatial distribution of risk remain heterogeneous. The recommended strategy is a regionally differentiated intervention combining post-exposure education, proximity-based dog vaccination, and targeted surveillance.

title_zh: 几内亚共和国 狂犬病 风险的一项健康优先事项:人类知识、犬类免疫和空间分析的整合

Associations were estimated by logistic regression with 95% confidence intervals, and spatial findings were displayed on a real map of Guinea. Results: Knowledge was insufficient or intermediate among most respondents, unfavorable attitudes reached 88.84%, and poor practices reached 73.80%. title: Organic waste mismanagement, free-roaming dog ecology, and rabies risk in endemic countries: a one health narrative review
abstract: Background Rabies remains a neglected tropical disease in many endemic regions of Asia and Africa, where dogs are the principal source of human rabies transmission. Poorly managed organic, household, food, and municipal solid waste can provide predictable food resources that support the survival, aggregation, and persistence of free-roaming dogs in human-dominated environments. Objective This narrative review aimed to synthesize evidence on how organic waste mismanagement supports free-roaming dog populations in rabies-endemic countries and how this environmental pathway may indirectly influence dog-bite risk, rabies exposure, and progress toward eliminating dog-mediated human rabies deaths by 2030. Methodology A structured search for peer-reviewed articles published in English between 2010 and 2026 was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Eligible studies addressed organic waste, free-roaming dog ecology, human–dog interactions, rabies, dog bite risk, surveillance, vaccination, dog population management, and One Health interventions. The evidence was organized into analytical themes and integrated using thematic narrative synthesis, with country-specific findings used to illustrate common patterns and contextual differences. Findings Household waste, market waste, restaurant waste, butcher shop waste, and open dumps were associated with dog presence, scavenging, aggregation, movement, and population persistence by providing accessible food resources. Human practices, including open waste disposal, intentional feeding, dog abandonment, and unrestricted dog ownership, further maintained dogs’ access to these resources. Waste-associated dog aggregation may increase opportunities for dog–dog and human–dog contact and complicate vaccination and humane population management programs. Rabies prevention was further constrained by incomplete vaccination coverage, inadequate dog population estimates, underreporting, limited or unequal access to post-exposure prophylaxis, weak surveillance, and insufficient intersectoral coordination. However, direct causal evidence that reducing accessible organic waste leads to reductions in dog density, dog-bite incidence, or rabies transmission remains limited. Conclusion Organic waste mismanagement is a neglected environmental pathway that may indirectly contribute to the risk of dog-mediated rabies. Waste management should complement mass dog vaccination, humane population management, responsible ownership, community education, surveillance, and timely postexposure prophylaxis within an integrated One Health framework.

title: Clinicodemographic Profile of Dog Bite Cases Presenting to the Emergency Medicine Department in a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Retrospective Observational Study
abstract: Background: Dog bites are a major public health concern and an important cause of presentation to emergency departments, particularly in regions where rabies remains endemic. Characterising the demographic profile, injury patterns, exposure severity, and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) practices may help improve emergency management and rabies prevention. Objective: To describe the demographic and clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution of dog-bite injuries, World Health Organization (WHO) exposure categories, PEP practices, and short-term hospital disposition among patients presenting with dog-bite injuries to a tertiary-care emergency department. Methods: A retrospective, observational, census-based study was conducted in the Department of Emergency Medicine, Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences, Faridabad, Haryana, India. Medical records of patients presenting with dog-bite injuries between January and December 2025 were reviewed. Data regarding age, sex, date of presentation, anatomical site of injury, type of biting dog, WHO exposure category, tetanus prophylaxis, anti-rabies vaccine (ARV), rabies immunoglobulin (RIG), and hospital disposition were extracted and analysed using descriptive statistics. Where appropriate, categorical variables were compared using the chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test. Results: Eighty-nine patients were included. The mean age was 32.34 ± 19.86 years, and 60 (67.4%) were male. Young adults aged 18–44 years constituted 51.7% of cases. Presentations peaked in June and July, accounting for 60.7% of cases. The lower limb was the most frequently affected anatomical site (38.2%), followed by the hand and fingers (29.2%). WHO Category III exposure predominated (59.6%), followed by Category II (36.0%) and Category I (4.5%). Stray dogs accounted for 76.4% of bites. Tetanus prophylaxis was administered to 91.0% of patients, ARV to all patients, and RIG to 94.3% of Category III patients. Overall, 97.8% were managed as outpatients and 2.2% required hospital admission. Conclusion: Dog-bite presentations predominantly involved young adult males and stray-dog exposures, with Category III injuries constituting the majority. PEP administration was high, although instances of ARV administration in Category I and RIG administration in Category II exposures warrant evaluation for guideline concordance. Long-term clinical outcomes were not assessed. Keywords: Dog Bites; Rabies; Post-Exposure Prophylaxis; Emergency Medical Services; Retrospective Studies; Wounds and Injuries.

source_records.abstract: Background: Dog bites are a major public health concern and an important cause of presentation to emergency departments, particularly in regions where rabies remains endemic. Characterising the demographic profile, injury patterns, exposure severity, and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) practices may help improve emergency management and rabies prevention. Objective: To describe the demographic and clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution of dog-bite injuries, World Health Organization (WHO) exposure categories, PEP practices, and short-term hospital disposition among patients presenting with dog-bite injuries to a tertiary-care emergency department. Methods: A retrospective, observational, census-based study was conducted in the Department of Emergency Medicine, Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences, Faridabad, Haryana, India. Medical records of patients presenting with dog-bite injuries between January and December 2025 were reviewed. Data regarding age, sex, date of presentation, anatomical site of injury, type of biting dog, WHO exposure category, tetanus prophylaxis, anti-rabies vaccine (ARV), rabies immunoglobulin (RIG), and hospital disposition were extracted and analysed using descriptive statistics. Where appropriate, categorical variables were compared using the chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test. Results: Eighty-nine patients were included. The mean age was 32.34 ± 19.86 years, and 60 (67.4%) were male. Young adults aged 18–44 years constituted 51.7% of cases. Presentations peaked in June and July, accounting for 60.7% of cases. The lower limb was the most frequently affected anatomical site (38.2%), followed by the hand and fingers (29.2%). WHO Category III exposure predominated (59.6%), followed by Category II (36.0%) and Category I (4.5%). Stray dogs accounted for 76.4% of bites. Tetanus prophylaxis was administered to 91.0% of patients, ARV to all patients, and RIG to 94.3% of Category III patients. Overall, 97.8% were managed as outpatients and 2.2% required hospital admission. Conclusion: Dog-bite presentations predominantly involved young adult males and stray-dog exposures, with Category III injuries constituting the majority. PEP administration was high, although instances of ARV administration in Category I and RIG administration in Category II exposures warrant evaluation for guideline concordance. Long-term clinical outcomes were not assessed. Keywords: Dog Bites; Rabies; Post-Exposure Prophylaxis; Emergency Medical Services; Retrospective Studies; Wounds and Injuries.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational study examined the clinicodemographic profile of dog bite cases presenting to an emergency department in India. The study included 89 patients, predominantly young adult males, with the lower limb being the most frequently affected site. WHO Category III exposure was most common, and stray dogs were the primary source of bites. High rates of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) were observed, though discrepancies in ARV and RIG administration across exposure categories were noted. Long-term outcomes were not assessed, indicating a gap in the evidence. The findings highlight the need for improved emergency management and rabies prevention strategies, particularly in addressing adherence to PEP guidelines and further investigating long-term clinical outcomes.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究旨在描述在三级护理急诊室就诊的狗咬伤患者的人口统计学和临床​​特征、狗咬伤的解剖学分布、世界卫生组织 (WHO) 暴露类别、暴露后预防 (PEP) 实践以及短期医院处置。重点是 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病,重点是人类病例及其管理。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 印度哈里亚纳邦法里达巴德阿姆里塔医学科学研究所急诊医学系进行了一项基于人口普查的回顾性观察性研究。对 2025 年 1 月至 12 月期间出现狗咬伤的患者的医疗记录进行了审查。提取有关年龄、性别、发病日期、受伤解剖部位、咬伤狗类型、WHO 暴露类别、破伤风预防、抗 狂犬病 疫苗 (ARV)、狂犬病 免疫球蛋白 (RIG) 和医院处置的数据,并使用描述性统计进行分析。使用卡方或 Fisher-Freeman-Halton 精确检验比较分类变量。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,共纳入 89 名患者,平均年龄为 32.34 ± 19.86 岁,其中 60 名患者(67.4%)为男性。下肢是最常受影响的解剖部位(38.2%),其次是手和手指(29.2%)。世卫组织 III 类暴露占主导地位 (59.6%),其次是 II 类 (36.0%) 和 I 类 (4.5%)。流浪狗咬伤事件占76.4%。91.0% 的患者接受破伤风预防,所有患者接受抗逆转录病毒治疗,94.3% 的 III 类患者接受 RIG 治疗。总体而言,97.8% 的患者接受门诊治疗,2.2% 的患者需要住院治疗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究指出,第一类暴露中的 ARV 管理和第二类暴露中的 RIG 管理实例值得评估指南的一致性。未评估长期临床结果,凸显了潜在的证据差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 描述人口概况、伤害模式、暴露严重程度和 暴露后预防 (PEP) 实践可能有助于改善应急管理和 暴露后预防 预防。研究结果表明,需要对长期临床结果进行进一步研究,并遵守不同 WHO 暴露类别的 PEP 管理指南。

title: Editorial: Cross-species transmission of viral infections
abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of zoonotic diseases represent a formidable and often unpredictable threat to global public health, as demonstrated by the devastating impact of recent viral outbreaks. These events are increasingly driven by a complex interplay of anthropogenic activities, human-animal coexistence, and enhanced global connectivity, which provide unprecedented opportunities for pathogen spillover and genetic recombination. Understanding the intricate mechanisms of viral dynamics at the human-animal-environment interface requires a multidisciplinary "One Health" approach that integrates robust genomic surveillance with spatial and epidemiological data. This Research Topic brings together nine high-impact studies that utilize advanced molecular and metagenomic tools to decipher the evolutionary trajectories of high-risk pathogens, ranging from well-established threats like Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and Influenza A to underappreciated viruses in wildlife and domestic reservoirs. By mapping transmission networks and identifying novel genetic variants, these contributions provide a proactive scientific foundation for pandemic preparedness and the development of effective biosecurity policies (Figure 1).Coronaviruses continue to be a primary focal point of genomic surveillance due to their broad host range and high propensity for genomic recombination and point mutations. Han and collaborators provide a critical "cross-species transmission alert" by documenting a novel recombinant coronavirus, TigerCoV-JL1, infecting a captive Amur tiger in China (Figure 1) (Han et al., 2026). Utilizing metagenomic next-generation sequencing, the researchers identified that this strain represents a unique canine-raccoon dog recombinant, carrying genetic signals from domestic canine coronaviruses and raccoon dog lineages within the ORF1a and Spike (S) genes. This discovery highlights the susceptibility of endangered felids to viral jumps and underscores the risks inherent in semi-captive environments where high-density interfaces between carnivores facilitate complex evolutionary pathways. In parallel, the study by Pan and colleagues delves into the molecular determinants of immune evasion within the merbecovirus subgenus.By evaluating ten anti-MERS-CoV monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against a diverse panel of pseudoviruses, they demonstrated how the V530L substitution in the MERS-CoV clade B, identified during the 2015 South Korean outbreak, drastically reduces the neutralization potency of the potent mAb m336 (Pan et al., 2025). Advanced structural modeling using AlphaFold3 revealed that this substitution induces significant steric changes in the receptor-binding domain (RBD), disrupting high-affinity hydrogen bonds between the antibody and the viral protein.These findings collectively emphasize that while large-scale recombination events expand host range, discrete molecular adaptations can compromise therapeutic efficacy, necessitating the development of multi-epitope strategies for future pandemic preparedness (Pan et al., 2025;Han et al., 2026).The role of domestic animals as "mixing vessels" for viral evolution remains a critical pillar of zoonotic risk assessment (Figure 1). Pigs, in particular, possess receptors for both avian and human influenza viruses, facilitating complex genetic reassortment, and the emergence of strains with pandemic potential. Cavicchio and associates exemplify the importance of sustained monitoring through a decade-long passive surveillance study (2013)(2014)(2015)(2016)(2017)(2018)(2019)(2020)(2021)(2022) in Northern Italy, which identified 12 distinct Swine Influenza A (swIAV) genotypes, including the first European reports of the Novel 1 and Novel 2 genotypes (Cavicchio et al., 2025). Their phylogenetic analysis revealed that genetic clustering is strongly influenced by anthropogenic factors, such as farm ownership and management practices, with documented instances of human-to-swine transmission sustaining local viral circulation and increasing the complexity of the internal gene constellations. Parallel surveillance in China by Zhao and coworkers characterized a novel triplereassortant H1N2 virus, designated as genotype G21, which acquired its HA gene from Eurasian avian-like H1N1 and its internal genes from the 2009 pandemic H1N1 (Zhao et al., 2026). Molecular analysis of this isolate identified the N31 substitution in the M2 protein, conferring adamantane resistance, and the S42 mutation in the NS1 protein, which is known to influence virulence in mammalian models. Furthermore, experimental infection in BALB/c mice confirmed moderate pathogenicity and efficient replication in the lungs and nasal turbinates, signaling its potential for further regional adaptation. Beyond respiratory threats, the study by Liu and collaborators underscores the significant food safety implications of the human-swine interface across Asia. By analyzing 348 complete genomes of Hepatitis E virus (HEV), they identified 34 recombination events, predominantly localized within the RdRp region, including 14 cross-species exchanges between swine and human strains (Liu et al., 2026). The high frequency of HEV-4 recombination in China appears to be driven by the intensive nature of the swine industry and high-density interaction hubs, reinforcing the need for stricter quarantine and molecular monitoring across the entire food production chain to mitigate the risk of zoonotic foodborne transmission (Liu et al., 2026;Zhao et al., 2026).Wildlife reservoirs serve as the primary origin of future pandemics, yet their internal viral landscapes often remain opaque. Huangfu and associates address this gap through an extensive metagenomic survey of the Asian house shrew (Suncus murinus) in tropical Hainan, China. By performing RNA sequencing on multiple tissues, the researchers identified a staggering 192 RNA viruses belonging to 32 known families, including significant human pathogens such as Henipavirus, Langat virus (LGTV), Amur virus (AMRV), and Influenza A (H1N1) (Huangfu et al., 2026). Their findings challenge the traditional perception of shrews as low-diversity reservoirs and identify them as a critical "ecological bridge" facilitating viral sharing between otherwise distantly related hosts, such as rodents and bats (Figure 1). This diversity is likely enhanced by the tropical ecosystem of Hainan, which supports stable host and vector populations year-round. In the avian sector, Tan and collaborator's provide critical insights into the taxonomy and distribution of pigeon gammacoronavirus (PgCoV). Utilizing high-throughput sequencing, they assembled a complete 27,538 nt genome, identifying unique accessory protein profiles, including a novel ORFx2 and the absence of proteins 3a and 3b (Tan et al., 2025). Comparative analysis of five conserved domains (including 3CLpro and RdRp) revealed amino acid differences exceeding 8.3% compared to known species, providing robust evidence for classifying PgCoV as a novel species within the genus Gammacoronavirus. Furthermore, their epidemiological survey documented a remarkably high flock-level prevalence of 97.73%, with RT-PCR evidence of viral replication in intestinal and kidney tissues, signaling the virus's potential pathogenicity in the digestive and urinary systems of pigeons. Collectively, these studies underscore the necessity of integrating understudied synanthropic and avian species into global virological surveillance to monitor emerging biosecurity threats (Tan et al., 2025;Huangfu et al., 2026).The complexity of viral dynamics is further elucidated by combining long-term field surveillance with human-centric molecular network analyses. Weinberg and associates provide a significant regional perspective from Israel, where 27 years of surveillance encompassing over 42,000 animals demonstrated a minimal risk of Rabies lyssavirus spillover from bats to terrestrial mammals (Weinberg et al., 2025). Despite the presence of 32 bat species, including the synanthropic Egyptian fruit bat which frequently forages in urban environments, zero positive cases were identified among the 294 bats tested using the historical gold-standard TAF method. This absence of infection reinforces the epidemiological distinction between Old and New World bat populations and highlights that reservoir roles are often region-specific, suggesting that bats in this region remain largely isolated from terrestrial Lyssavirus transmission cycles. In contrast, in the context of direct human-to-human transmission, Wu and colleagues utilize molecular transmission networks to track HIV-1 among men who have sex with men (MSM) in Ningxia, China. Their analysis of 296 pol gene sequences revealed an overall clustering rate of 43.6%, with the CRF07_BC subtype (57.1%) emerging as a dominant driver of localized spread (Wu et al., 2026). Notably, the study identified an alarming 38.2% prevalence of acquired drug resistance among sequenced individuals, demanding targeted public health interventions based on urban spatial connectivity and a "network-based approach" to effectively manage the spread of the epidemic. These contrasting studies emphasize that while some natural reservoirs pose low immediate risks, human social networks remain high-velocity conduits for viral dissemination and evolution (Weinberg et al., 2025;Wu et al., 2026).In conclusion, the studies presented in this Research Topic reaffirm that genomic surveillance is a proactive sentinel for global health security rather than merely a descriptive tool.By integrating data across the human-animal-environment interface, researchers have mapped recombination hotspots in Hepatitis E and swIAV, identified cross-species transmission potential in felid coronaviruses, and defined novel species of avian gammacoronaviruses. These contributions provide a robust scientific foundation for evidence-based biosecurity and public health policies, highlighting that discrete molecular adaptations can significantly compromise therapeutic efficacy or alter pathogenicity. The adoption of a multidisciplinary "One Health" framework is essential to stay ahead of viral adaptation, particularly as anthropogenic activities and ecological shifts continue to blur the boundaries between domestic and wild habitats.Ultimately, this collection underscores that protecting global biodiversity, ensuring food safety, and monitoring high-risk human networks are intrinsically linked strategies for the mitigation of future pandemic threats in an ever-changing world. The diagram illustrates the interconnectedness of wildlife (e.g., Amur tigers, Asian house shrews, and bats), domestic animals (e.g., swine and pigeons), and humans in the transmission and evolution of viral pathogens. Key evolutionary drivers, such as genomic recombination and reassortment, are highlighted as mechanisms for host-jumping and therapeutic evasion. Arrows represent documented or potential viral spillover pathways and transmission networks identified by the contributing studies in this Research Topic.

This Research Topic brings together nine high-impact studies that utilize advanced molecular and metagenomic tools to decipher the evolutionary trajectories of high-risk pathogens, ranging from well-established threats like Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and Influenza A to underappreciated viruses in wildlife and domestic reservoirs. Han and collaborators provide a critical "cross-species transmission alert" by documenting a novel recombinant coronavirus, TigerCoV-JL1, infecting a captive Amur tiger in China (Figure 1) (Han et al., 2026). Utilizing metagenomic next-generation sequencing, the researchers identified that this strain represents a unique canine-raccoon dog recombinant, carrying genetic signals from domestic canine coronaviruses and raccoon dog lineages within the ORF1a and Spike (S) genes. This discovery highlights the susceptibility of endangered felids to viral jumps and underscores the risks inherent in semi-captive environments where high-density interfaces between carnivores facilitate complex evolutionary pathways. In parallel, the study by Pan and colleagues delves into the molecular determinants of immune evasion within the merbecovirus subgenus.By evaluating ten anti-MERS-CoV monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against a diverse panel of pseudoviruses, they demonstrated how the V530L substitution in the MERS-CoV clade B, identified during the 2015 South Korean outbreak, drastically reduces the neutralization potency of the potent mAb m336 (Pan et al., 2025). Pigs, in particular, possess receptors for both avian and human influenza viruses, facilitating complex genetic reassortment, and the emergence of strains with pandemic potential. Cavicchio and associates exemplify the importance of sustained monitoring through a decade-long passive surveillance study (2013)(2014)(2015)(2016)(2017)(2018)(2019)(2020)(2021)(2022) in Northern Italy, which identified 12 distinct Swine Influenza A (swIAV) genotypes, including the first European reports of the Novel 1 and Novel 2 genotypes (Cavicchio et al., 2025). Their phylogenetic analysis revealed that genetic clustering is strongly influenced by anthropogenic factors, such as farm ownership and management practices, with documented instances of human-to-swine transmission sustaining local viral circulation and increasing the complexity of the internal gene constellations. Parallel surveillance in China by Zhao and coworkers characterized a novel triplereassortant H1N2 virus, designated as genotype G21, which acquired its HA gene from Eurasian avian-like H1N1 and its internal genes from the 2009 pandemic H1N1 (Zhao et al., 2026). Molecular analysis of this isolate identified the N31 substitution in the M2 protein, conferring adamantane resistance, and the S42 mutation in the NS1 protein, which is known to influence virulence in mammalian models. Furthermore, experimental infection in BALB/c mice confirmed moderate pathogenicity and efficient replication in the lungs and nasal turbinates, signaling its potential for further regional adaptation. Beyond respiratory threats, the study by Liu and collaborators underscores the significant food safety implications of the human-swine interface across Asia. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the growing threat of zoonotic diseases, particularly rabies virus, by examining the mechanisms of cross-species transmission and the role of genetic recombination in expanding host range and creating new public health risks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The editorial compiles nine high-impact studies, including those on rabies virus, coronaviruses, swine influenza, and Hepatitis E virus, focusing on their transmission dynamics across different host species and environments.
analysis.methods: The studies employ metagenomic next-generation sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, structural modeling, and epidemiological surveys to investigate viral evolution, transmission patterns, and genetic adaptations in various host species.
analysis.main_results: The research highlights the emergence of a novel recombinant coronavirus, TigerCoV-JL1, in a captive Amur tiger, and identifies molecular adaptations in MERS-CoV and swine influenza viruses that affect immune evasion and therapeutic efficacy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings emphasize that while large-scale recombination events expand host range, discrete molecular adaptations can significantly impact therapeutic efficacy, necessitating the development of multi-epitope strategies for pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the need for enhanced genomic surveillance in domestic animals and wildlife reservoirs, as well as stricter biosecurity measures to prevent zoonotic transmission and mitigate public health risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is primarily based on abstract-level descriptions, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the studies are high-impact and provide robust insights into viral dynamics and cross-species transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial compiles nine high-impact studies on cross-species viral transmission, emphasizing the role of genetic recombination and molecular adaptations in expanding host range and creating new public health risks. The research highlights the emergence of a novel recombinant coronavirus in a captive Amur tiger and identifies molecular changes in MERS-CoV and swine influenza viruses that affect immune evasion and therapeutic efficacy. These findings underscore the importance of genomic surveillance in domestic animals and wildlife reservoirs, as well as the need for multi-epitope strategies in pandemic preparedness. The studies also reveal the significance of the swine industry and tropical ecosystems in facilitating viral recombination and transmission. While the evidence is abstract-level, the insights are robust and relevant for understanding zoonotic threats. The editorial calls for integrating understudied species into global virological surveillance to better monitor emerging biosecurity risks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究通过研究跨物种 传播 的机制以及基因重组在扩大 宿主 范围和创造新的公共卫生风险中的作用,解决了人畜共患疾病日益严重的威胁,特别是 狂犬病病毒。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该社论汇编了九项高影响力的研究,包括关于 狂犬病病毒、冠状病毒、猪流感和戊型肝炎病毒的研究,重点关注它们在不同 宿主 物种和环境中的 传播 动态。
elements_zh.methods: 这些研究采用宏基因组下一代测序、系统发育分析、结构建模和流行病学调查来研究病毒 进化、传播 模式以及各种 宿主 物种的遗传适应。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究强调了在圈养东北虎中出现的一种新型重组冠状病毒 TigerCoV-JL1,并确定了 MERS-CoV 和猪流感病毒中影响免疫逃避和治疗效果的分子适应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,虽然大规模重组事件扩大了 宿主 范围,但离散的分子适应可以显着影响治疗效果,因此需要开发多表位策略来预防大流行。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明需要加强家畜和野生动物的 基因组监测,以及更严格的生物安全措施,以预防人畜共患 传播 并减轻公共卫生风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据主要基于抽象级别的描述,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,这些研究影响很大,为病毒动力学和跨物种 传播 提供了深入的见解。

研究 (2013)(2014)(2015)(2016)(2017)(2018)(2019)(2020)(2021)(2022) 举例说明了持续监测的重要性,该研究确定了 12 种不同的甲型猪流感 (swIAV)基因型,包括欧洲首次报告 Novel 1 和 Novel 2 基因型(Cavicchio 等,2025)。他们的系统发育分析表明,遗传聚类受到人为因素的强烈影响,例如农场所有权和管理实践,有记录的人传猪 传播 的实例维持了局部病毒循环并增加了内部基因群的复杂性。赵和同事在中国进行的平行 监测 表征了一种新型三重重组 H1N2 病毒,命名为基因型 G21,其 HA 基因来自欧亚类禽 H1N1,其内部基因来自 2009 年大流行的 H1N1(Zhao 等人,2026)。对该分离株的分子分析鉴定出 M2 蛋白中的 N31 取代,赋予金刚烷抗性,以及 NS1 蛋白中的 S42 突变,已知 NS1 会影响哺乳动物模型中的毒力。此外,BALB/c 小鼠的实验感染证实了其在肺部和鼻甲中具有中等致病性和有效复制,这表明其具有进一步区域适应的潜力。除了呼吸道威胁之外,刘和合作者的研究还强调了整个亚洲人与猪接触对食品安全的重大影响。通过分析 348 个完整的戊型肝炎病毒 (HEV) 基因组,他们鉴定了 34 个重组事件,主要位于 RdRp 区域,其中包括猪和人毒株之间的 14 个跨物种交换(Liu 等人,2026)。中国HEV-4重组的高频率似乎是由养猪业的集约性和高密度互动中心推动的,这强化了在整个食品生产链中进行更严格的检疫和分子监测的必要性,以减轻人畜共患食源性传播的风险(Liu等人,2026;Zhao等人,2026)。野生动物储存宿主是未来流行病的主要起源,但他们的内部病毒景观通常仍然不透明。皇甫及其同事通过对中国热带海南省的亚洲家鼩(Suncus murinus)进行广泛的宏基因组调查来解决这一差距。通过对多个组织进行RNA测序,研究人员鉴定出了属于32个已知科的惊人的192种RNA病毒,其中包括重要的人类病原体,例如亨尼帕病毒、兰加特病毒(LGTV)、阿穆尔病毒(AMRV)和甲型流感(H1N1)(Huangfu et al.,2026)。他们的发现挑战了鼩鼱作为低多样性 储存宿主 的传统观念,并将它们视为重要的“生态桥梁”,促进其他关系较远的 宿主(例如啮齿动物和蝙蝠)之间的病毒共享(图 1)。海南的热带生态系统可能增强了这种多样性,该生态系统全年支持稳定的 宿主 和 媒介 种群。在禽类领域,Tan 和合作者对鸽子伽马冠状病毒 (PgCoV) 的分类和分布提供了重要见解。利用高通量测序,他们组装了完整的 27,538 nt 基因组,识别了独特的辅助蛋白谱,包括新的 ORFx2 以及蛋白 3a 和 3b 的缺失(Tan 等人,2025)。对五个保守结构域(包括 3CLpro 和 RdRp)的比较分析显示,与已知物种相比,氨基酸差异超过 8.3%,为将 PgCoV 分类为 Gamma 冠状病毒属中的新物种提供了有力的证据。此外,他们的流行病学调查记录了鸡群患病率的水平非常高,达到97.73%,RT-PCR证据表明病毒在肠道和肾脏组织中复制,表明该病毒在鸽子的消化和泌尿系统中具有潜在的致病性。总的来说,这些研究强调了将未充分研究的共生物种和鸟类物种整合到全球病毒学 监测 中的必要性,以监测新兴的生物安全威胁(Tan 等,2025;Huangfu 等,2026)。通过将长期现场 监测 与以人为中心的分子网络分析相结合,进一步阐明了病毒动力学的复杂性。Weinberg 及其同事提供了来自以色列的重要区域视角,其中 27 年的 监测 涵盖超过 42,000 只动物,证明 狂犬病 狂犬病病毒 跨物种溢出 从蝙蝠传播到陆地哺乳动物的风险极小(Weinberg 等人,2025)。尽管存在 32 种蝙蝠,包括经常在城市环境中觅食的埃及果蝠,但在使用历史金标准 TAF 方法测试的 294 只蝙蝠中,发现了零阳性病例。这种没有感染的情况强化了旧世界和新世界蝙蝠种群之间的流行病学差异,并强调了 储存宿主 的作用通常是区域特异性的,这表明该地区的蝙蝠在很大程度上与陆地狂犬病病毒 传播 循环隔离。相比之下,在直接人传人 传播 的背景下,Wu 及其同事利用分子 传播 网络来追踪中国宁夏男男性行为者 (MSM) 中的 HIV-1。他们对 296 个 pol 基因序列的分析显示,总体聚类率为 43.6%,其中 CRF07_BC 亚型 (57.1%) 成为局部传播的主要驱动因素 (Wu et al.,2026)。值得注意的是,该研究发现,测序个体中获得性耐药率达到惊人的38.2% 患病率,需要基于城市空间连通性和“基于网络的方法”进行有针对性的公共卫生干预,以有效管理疫情的传播。这些对比研究强调,虽然一些自然的 储存宿主 的直接风险较低,但人类社交网络仍然是病毒传播和 进化 的高速渠道(Weinberg 等人,2025;Wu 等人,2026)。总之,本研究主题中提出的研究重申,基因组监测 是全球健康安全的主动哨兵,而不仅仅是描述性工具。通过整合数据在人类与动物环境界面上,研究人员绘制了戊型肝炎和 swIAV 的重组热点,确定了猫科动物冠状病毒的跨物种 传播 潜力,并定义了禽类伽马冠状病毒的新物种。这些贡献为基于证据的生物安全和公共卫生政策提供了坚实的科学基础,强调离散的分子适应可能会显着损害治疗效果或改变致病性。采用多学科的“同一个健康”框架对于保持病毒适应的领先地位至关重要,特别是在人类活动和生态变化继续模糊国内和野生栖息地之间的界限的情况下。最终,该系列强调了保护全球生物多样性、确保食品安全和监测高风险人类网络是在不断变化的世界中减轻未来流行病威胁的内在联系策略。该图说明了野生动物(例如东北虎、亚洲家鼩和蝙蝠)、家畜(例如猪和鸽子)和人类在病毒病原体 传播 和 进化 中的相互关联性。关键的进化驱动因素,例如基因组重组和重配,被强调为 宿主 跳跃和治疗逃避的机制。箭头代表本研究主题中的贡献研究确定的已记录或潜在的病毒 跨物种溢出 途径和 传播 网络。

analysis_zh.methods: 这些研究采用宏基因组下一代测序、系统发育分析、结构建模和流行病学调查来研究病毒 进化、传播 模式以及各种 宿主 物种的遗传适应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究强调了在圈养东北虎中出现的一种新型重组冠状病毒 TigerCoV-JL1,并确定了 MERS-CoV 和猪流感病毒中影响免疫逃避和治疗效果的分子适应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,虽然大规模重组事件扩大了 宿主 范围,但离散的分子适应可以显着影响治疗效果,因此需要开发多表位策略来预防大流行。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明需要加强家畜和野生动物的 基因组监测,以及更严格的生物安全措施,以预防人畜共患 传播 并减轻公共卫生风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据主要基于抽象级别的描述,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,这些研究影响很大,为病毒动力学和跨物种 传播 提供了深入的见解。

title: Viral PDZ target sequences are not inherently more promiscuous than those derived from endogenous target proteins.
abstract: PDZ domains are one of the largest families of short linear motif (or peptide) binding domains in the human proteome. These scaffolding domains are important in signaling and trafficking pathways, such as in the formation of tight junctions or in the postsynaptic density of neurons. PDZ domains are also targeted by several pathogenic viral proteins, including human papillomavirus (HPV), influenza, hepatitis, rabies, coronaviruses, among others. Previously, we investigated the specificity determinants of modulator, or non-motif, residues for two PDZ binding motifs (or PBMs) from the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) and HPV16 E6 proteins to better understand differences in relative promiscuity between these similar sequences. To test whether viral PDZ-binding motifs are inherently more promiscuous than endogenous targets, we measured binding affinities for 7 endogenous and 7 viral PBMs across 8 well-studied Class I PDZ domains. Fluorescence anisotropy assays revealed no significant difference in relative binding affinities between viral and endogenous PBMs, indicating that viral versus endogenous origin alone does not explain PBM promiscuity. Our results were consistent with available data from high throughput holdup assays. Taken together, our data support previously reported sequence hotspots, whereby certain PBMs are recognized by large numbers of PDZ domains, likely due to a combination of widely favorable modulator residues.

These scaffolding domains are important in signaling and trafficking pathways, such as in the formation of tight junctions or in the postsynaptic density of neurons. PDZ domains are also targeted by several pathogenic viral proteins, including human papillomavirus (HPV), influenza, hepatitis, rabies, coronaviruses, among others. Previously, we investigated the specificity determinants of modulator, or non-motif, residues for two PDZ binding motifs (or PBMs) from the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) and HPV16 E6 proteins to better understand differences in relative promiscuity between these similar sequences. To test whether viral PDZ-binding motifs are inherently more promiscuous than endogenous targets, we measured binding affinities for 7 endogenous and 7 viral PBMs across 8 well-studied Class I PDZ domains. Fluorescence anisotropy assays revealed no significant difference in relative binding affinities between viral and endogenous PBMs, indicating that viral versus endogenous origin alone does not explain PBM promiscuity. Our results were consistent with available data from high throughput holdup assays. title: Complete reference genomes track disease notoriety, not burden: a burden–genome mismatch for priority zoonoses along China's land border
abstract: Abstract Complete reference genomes are essential for molecular diagnosis, typing, and source-tracing; yet their availability for the zoonoses that cause the greatest disease burden is seldom assessed. Along China's land border, where a heterogeneous set of priority zoonoses circulates, we investigated whether complete reference-genome resources correspond to disease burden. For 15 border-priority zoonoses, we compiled disease burden (using notifiable-disease cases from China CDC and animal events from WAHIS), complete-genome availability (from NCBI), and research output (from PubMed) as a secondary metric. We evaluated the relationship between burden and genome availability and verified its robustness using different genome metrics, a leave-one-out jackknife procedure, an exact permutation test, and alternative burden definitions, while also revealing a genome-metric paradox. Among the six diseases with official Chinese human-incidence data, complete reference genomes exhibited a strong inverse correlation with burden (Spearman ρ = −0.94; exact permutation p = 0.001): brucellosis, the highest-burden zoonosis (67 418 cases in 2024), had only 4 complete genomes, whereas low-burden rabies (170 cases) had 2 740. This relationship remained stable when excluding any single disease (ρ = −0.90 to −1.0), incorporating animal burden (ρ = −0.89), or employing a viral-record metric. Importantly, the association depended on the use of complete genomes: total assembly counts (which include numerous draft genomes) yielded an opposite correlation ρ = +0.71. Thus, the finding pertains specifically to finished-quality reference genomes rather than total sequencing efforts, and we explicitly report this paradox. The high-burden, genome-poor group included both bacterial and viral pathogens, precluding a taxonomic artefact. Research output (uncapped PubMed totals) showed no significant relationship with burden (ρ = −0.26, p = 0.6). Nine of the 15 border zoonoses lacked any official Chinese human-incidence data. Conclusions: Along China's border, complete reference genomes for priority zoonoses reflect pathogen notoriety rather than disease burden. Investment in finished reference genomes for high-burden, genome-poor zoonoses such as brucellosis would enhance their molecular diagnosis, typing, and source-tracing capabilities.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决理解人畜共患病的完整参考 基因组 是否与其疾病负担相符的差距,因为分子 诊断 和来源追踪依赖于此类资源,但很少根据负担指标评估其可用性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究重点关注中国陆地边界沿线的 15 种重点人畜共患病,研究其疾病负担与完整参考 基因组 的可用性之间的关系。它包括细菌和病毒病原体,确保潜在人畜共患病的多样化表现。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员汇编了中国法定疾病病例和动物事件的疾病负担数据、NCBI 的完整 基因组 可用性以及 PubMed 的研究成果。他们使用统计方法评估了负担和 基因组 可用性之间的关系,包括留一折刀法、精确排列测试和替代负担定义。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在中国官方人类 发病率 数据的六种疾病中,完整参考 基因组 显示与负担呈很强的负相关(Spearman ρ = -0.94;精确排列 p = 0.001)。布鲁氏菌病是负担最高的人兽共患病,只有4个完整的基因组,而负担较低的疾病狂犬病有2,740个。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,优先人畜共患疾病的完整参考 基因组 反映的是恶名而不是负担,突显了一个悖论,即高负担疾病的完整 基因组 较少,而且即使排除个别疾病或纳入动物负担,这种关系仍然保持稳定。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对布鲁氏菌病等高负担、基因组 缺乏的人畜共患病,投资完整的参考 基因组 可以改善分子 基因组、分型和来源追踪,这对于有效的公共卫生应对措施至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据基于仅摘要数据,并使用统计方法评估了负担与 基因组 可用性之间的关系。研究发现这种关联依赖于完整 基因组 的使用,而不是总测序工作,这限制了对其他上下文的普遍适用性。

title: Territorial expansion and parasitic zoonoses: the pampas gray fox in Argentina as a case study and its educational potential for prevention
abstract: According to Santos and Tellería (2006), these types of processes have numerous consequences: regional habitat loss and the resulting reduction in the size of affected organism populations, decreasing the regional density of species; an increase in the distance between fragments, hindering the exchange of individuals between isolated populations for the purpose of replenishment; and greater exposure of the fragmented habitat to multiple interferences from surrounding habitats (habitat matrix), resulting in a growing "edge effect" that causes a decline in habitat quality, affecting the survival of populations residing in the fragments. The reduction, fragmentation, and deterioration of habitat ultimately lead to the atomization of original distributions into increasingly smaller and more isolated subpopulations, resulting, in situations where the problem progresses unabated, in landscapes where many of the original species are missing (Santos and Tellería, 2006).Considering the "One Health" approach, it is important to understand that this environmental impact and its consequences for animal habitats also create problems for the surrounding communities or even those that live alongside them. This is because human-animal relationships become more complex with each generation. Although animals continue to fulfill a utilitarian role in human life (the food industry, animal breeding and sales, among others), they are affected by the environmental controls implemented by humanity due to their susceptibility (Gutiérrez et al., 2007). This leads to a normalization, evolution, and narrowing of human-animal interaction with species that should not be in this situation. These species are influenced by territorial transformations, human convenience, and also by the affectionate relationships that develop with them due to the insensitivity caused by convenience, ignorance, or ideology (Gutiérrez et al., 2007;Santos and Tellería, 2006). However, this also has negative consequences for human beings. (2022) state, these situations carry risks for the community, such as zoonoses, consequences that arise from compromising or threatening the environment. This creates conditions that foster a breeding ground for disease by making it unhealthy for life, since human health is not independent of the health of other organisms. This is where the importance of a comprehensive approach that considers all the components of One Health comes in (Lampert et al., 2022).Understanding the importance of the integrity of all actors within a community allows for a different perspective on the relevance of territorial transformations and urban planning to health risks. The approach of canids to urban areas is directly related to anthropogenic processes. Temporal interactions and competition between species even arise depending on variables such as housing density and forest cover (Pearson et al., 2022). The consequences of urbanization, which accompany changes in land use, the incorporation of substances to enhance soil productivity, and habitat loss and fragmentation, modify the distribution of carnivorous mammals (Pereira et al., 2024). Furthermore, the potential consumption of these animals by humans is another factor that can influence the presence of wild mammals in areas currently inhabited by humans (Pereira et al., 2024;Lampert, 2025). All these factors contribute to the loss of biodiversity, which is accompanied by the loss of natural habitats, the reorganization of communities (Pereira et al., 2025), and the nutritional and metabolic problems associated with the intake of ultra-processed foods that are typical of human beings (Lampert, 2025).Human activities that influence the interaction of canids are affected by their sensitivity. This sensitivity to humans was demonstrated during the COVID-19 pandemic. One study showed that gray foxes (Urocyon cinereoargenteus), red foxes (Vulpes vulpes), and coyotes (Canis latrans) modified their daily activities in both urban and rural areas (Allen et al., 2025). Gray foxes modified their daily activities in rural areas, while coyotes modified theirs in urban areas (Allen et al., 2025). Gray foxes were the canids that exhibited the greatest change in daily activity during the pandemic (Allen et al., 2025).For example, the Pampas gray fox (Lycalopex gymnocercus) is one of the most widespread and abundant wild canids in Argentina. However, it is common to see news reports of this species being found in urban areas. This can pose a potential risk for the transmission of parasitic zoonotic diseases. A study conducted in the Province of Buenos Aires found that of 142 foxes found dead and/or captured, the digestive tract harbored 16 species of helminths (4 cestodes, 1 trematode, and 11 nematodes) and 9 species of protozoa (Scioscia, 2022). Furthermore, the Pampas gray fox is a host for E. bohemi (Scioscia et al., 2018). Furthermore, another study mentions the presence of Neospora caninum in the animal. This is of great concern given that it is a protozoan that causes abortions and reproductive failures in livestock, resulting in significant economic losses (Scioscia et al., 2022). In Argentina, there are various reports of the appearance of the pampas gray fox in urban and rural areas inhabited by people. Urban expansion into natural habitats is leading to increasingly close contact between humans and native wildlife, which can result in the transmission of zoonotic diseases. Given this situation, education plays a crucial role in prevention.The Pampas gray fox is of great ecological importance. Its role as a predator, scavenger, frugivore, and seed disperser has contributed to the development of diverse biomes (Vidal et al., 2025). This animal is a clear example of the importance of One Health education, based on the One Health approach. From an educational perspective, the Science, Technology, and Society (STS) approach is a valuable tool for fostering critical thinking in students, contextualizing learning, and enabling the community to understand different perspectives on an animal. Lampert (2025) has written a book titled "When the Jungle Sits Down to Eat," which analyzes how the welfare of coatis (Nasua nasua), the prevalence of zoonoses, and their behavior are affected by human interaction in Iguazu National Park (Misiones Province, Argentina). Previous research has demonstrated that classroom-based approaches to animal ecology, behavior, welfare, and health risks foster the development of critical thinking skills to prevent contact (Lampert, 2025). While this research focused on the coati, it is essential to address this educational topic with each species that arrives in urban areas, focusing on prevention. Furthermore, various interviews and studies have shown that people become more aware of the potential negative effects of interaction on the animal, rather than on themselves. Therefore, One Health education for prevention must focus not only on people, but also on the risk to species.For the Pampas gray fox, the issue of domestic dogs (Canis familiaris) is a factor within the broader context of habitat alteration. It is important to note that foxes are evolutionarily similar to domestic dogs, not only in terms of anatomy and physiology but also behavior (Fuchs et al., 2009). Peri-urban areas can serve as potential hotspots for pathogen exposure among dog and fox populations; consequently, both domestic dogs and wild foxes may be exposed to the same diseases. The presence of dogs in livestock and rural areas, combined with the encroachment of foxes into these zones (driven by habitat fragmentation and poor waste management) turns these interactions into a transmission pathway for pathogens of veterinary and public health significance (Fuchs et al., 2009).Recent research cites a case in Brazil where domestic dogs may act as bridge hosts for Rickettsia parkeri, transporting infected tick vectors from areas shared with wild foxes (the natural hosts) to vulnerable human populations (Hernández et al., 2021). The same authors who cited the case in Brazil conducted a survey in Chile, finding a higher number of dog-fox interactions (60 interactions) at a coastal peri-urban site compared to two other, less disturbed sites (12 interactions) (Hernández et al., 2021). Societal culture, animal husbandry practices, dietary habits, education levels, conditions of poverty and social marginalization, the availability of potable water, and the rural or urban nature of the habitat are variables that influence the epidemiological complex of various zoonoses (Samartino & Eddi, 2010). Populations in rural and peri-urban areas are in close contact with animals (often involving intensive rearing practices) resulting in significantly higher exposure. Furthermore, the Pampas gray fox frequently ventures into these areas due to their proximity to its natural habitat. Consequently, the level of risk differs between urban and rural zones, although the recent expansion of gated communities has narrowed this gap. It is also worth noting that many canids in rural areas often feed on animal offal; this practice can increase the risk of pathogen transmission to other species-such as the Pampas gray fox-and even directly to humans. Similarly, in urban and periurban spaces, population overcrowding in both zones increases the likelihood of disease transmission and epidemic outbreaks in many regions (Samartino & Eddi, 2010). In the context of territorial expansion, the creation of new neighborhoods in peri-urban areas has facilitated the transmission of various zoonotic diseases to the human population (Samartino & Eddi, 2010).The presence of protozoa (T. caninum), bacteria (Leptospira spp., Brucella spp., antimicrobial-resistant Enterococcus spp.), and viruses (rabies) illustrates how the Pampas gray fox facilitates pathogen transmission (Vidal et al., 2025). Therefore, the Pampas fox should be viewed less as a simple reservoir and more as an indicator of ecological dysfunction, given that health risks are typically associated with transmission via uncontrolled domestic animals rather than the species itself (Vidal et al., 2025). Therefore, the aim is to improve understanding of the spatiotemporal patterns of interspecific contact between invasive and native carnivores, in order to prevent the spread of various pathogens (Hernández et al., 2021). Consequently, education is a fundamental aspect of preventing such transmission. It is worth noting that this education must be contextualized within the specific settings where pathogen transmission is likely to occur. Hence the importance of raising awareness about zoonoses in the various spaces shared by humans and animals, as well as among different animal species. The interaction between animals, humans, and their habitats should be a central focus of modern scientific education; the goal is not merely to learn the definitions and characteristics of various zoonoses, but to understand the environments in which transmission takes place. This enables the public to become informed-for instance, on how to act when encountering animals.In the case of the Pampas Gray Fox, human intervention is impacting its ecology through the use of poison, hunting, roads, and urbanization. This leads us to consider this animal as a model for understanding the capacity to govern shared life with integrity, maintaining ecological and health functions in balance (Vidal et al., 2025). Therefore, education must promote conservation by raising awareness of the human-caused problems affecting this animal and their potential solutions, such as banning poisons, reducing roadkill, managing domestic animals, and promoting coexistence under a genuine "One Health, One Wellbeing" approach, as described by Vidal et al. (2025), in order to achieve the integration of human, animal, and environmental health in urban planning.The STS approach to one health prevention education should incorporate the following elements, drawing on the book of Lampert (2019): Mainstream the "One Health, One Wellbeing" or Conservation Medicine approach. In the case of the Pampas gray fox, education regarding the animal should not be conducted in isolation-treating the animal's physiology and habitat, zoonoses, and territorial/urban expansion as separate topics. Instead, the issue must be addressed through an integrated, cross-cutting approach that acknowledges its complexity.  Contextualize instruction across different settings. Studying and understanding human-animal contact differs depending on whether the setting is rural, peri-urban, or urban. Local wildlife must be identified, along with the ways in which the transmission of microorganisms between species could be altered.  Teach about animal feeding practices. It is essential to understand the risks posed to the ecosystem by feeding domestic canids animal offal or raw meat that has not undergone sanitary or food safety inspection.  Develop educational initiatives grounded in health education, environmental education, and food education. In the case of Argentina, it is worth noting that environmental education and food education are mandated by law.
